marks.gloss_en: מאי הוי עלה? תא שמע: דתניא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר אומר: שמן כדי לסוך אבר קטן של קטן בן יומו -- a tanna states the school of R' Yannai's measure in its very words (and so RSbE is not as the dechiya construed him)
(dechiya) R' Shimon ben Elazar holds a small limb of an adult and a large limb of a day-old child are alike
the mishna: and [the measure for carrying out] all other liquids is a revi'it
the stated measures apply to one who carries out [without storing]
אטו מצניע לאו מוציא הוא? -- is the one who stores not also one who carries out? then why does the baraita set him apart from the one who carries out?

הכא במאי עסקינן -- the baraita speaks of a student clearing his teacher's place for a meal: his liability for an insignificant item turns on whether his teacher stored it (= p_abaye_talmid and its three rulings)
Abaye: the baraita deals with a student whose teacher told him to clear the place for a meal, and he went and cleared it
one who carries out rope: enough to make a handle for a basket
כדשמואל, דאמר שמואל: כל שקייני מסו ומטללי לבר ממיא דמסו ולא מטללי
אלא מים, מכדי שתייתו שכיחא רפואתו לא שכיחא, מאי טעמא אזול רבנן בתר רפואתו לחומרא? -- by the rule, water should be measured by its common use, drinking, not by the eye-salve
רבא אמר: אפילו תימא בשאר מקומות, כדשמואל -- water's healing use is common too, so the 'common and common' half of the rule applies (= p_mayim_refuato_shechicha)
water: its drinking is common and its healing use is not
the mishna: [the measure for carrying out] water is enough to rub a kilor [eye salve] with it
wine: its drinking is common, its healing use not -- the Rabbis followed its drinking, which is common, to be lenient
שופכין למאי חזו? -- לגבל בהן את הטיט: waste water is fit for kneading clay, which is why carrying it out is measured
והתניא: טיט כדי לעשות בהן פי כור -- a baraita measures clay by what makes the mouth of a crucible

לא קשיא: הא דמיגבל, הא דלא מיגבל -- the baraita speaks of kneaded clay, R' Yirmeya of clay not yet kneaded, since no one troubles to knead clay for a crucible's mouth (= p_tit_okimta_megubal, p_shofchin_okimta_lo_megubal, p_ein_adam_toreach)
R' Yirmeya: waste waters are fit for kneading clay
